Thanks so much, Kai.

 

Narsing, we had a meeting yesterday about it (Kai, Meg, Ron, Mradul, and I) and the consensus was that there are a few options, such as using an API that wasn’t available back when Great Lakes started, and that we should start with talking to the business (Ryan Brandt) to make this is being driven by the business and that we understand their requirements. I was going to set up a meeting with Joel, Ryan, and I.

 

~Amy

"Below is the sql:
select a.table_catalog,a.table_schema,a.act_table_name,a.column_name,a.data_type,
b.table_catalog full_table_catalog,b.table_schema full_table_schema,b.act_table_name full_act_table_name,b.column_name full_column_name,b.data_type full_data_type,
c.table_catalog cdc_table_catalog,c.table_schema cdc_table_schema,c.act_table_name cdc_act_table_name,c.column_name cdc_column_name,c.data_type cdc_data_type
from
(select  table_catalog, table_schema, rtrim('_ods', table_name) as  table_name, table_name as act_table_name,  column_name, data_type from dev_sdh_db.information_schema.columns where table_schema='sapecc' and table_name like '%_ods') a  left join  
(select  table_catalog, table_schema, rtrim('_ods_full', table_name) as table_name, table_name as act_table_name, column_name, data_type from dev_sdh_db.information_schema.columns where table_schema='sapecc' and table_name like '%_ods_full') b  on
a.table_catalog = b.table_catalog and  a.table_schema=b.table_schema and  a.table_name=b.table_name and  a.column_name=b.column_name
left join    
(select  table_catalog, table_schema,rtrim('_ods_cdc', table_name) as  table_name, table_name as act_table_name, column_name, data_type from dev_sdh_db.information_schema.columns where table_schema='sapecc' and table_name like '%_ods_cdc') c   on
a.table_catalog = c.table_catalog and  a.table_schema=c.table_schema and  a.table_name=c.table_name and  a.column_name=c.column_name "

13/May/25 6:05 AM;712020:78b0c179-9e9a-4a11-8416-ef7cde9ed9f4;*Snowflake’s Default Behaviour*: Snowflake uses VARCHAR as its primary string data type, equivalent to STRING in other systems like Databricks. The (16777216) specifies the maximum length in bytes, which is Snowflake's default for VARCHAR when no length is explicitly defined. This ensures that the column can handle the largest possible string from the source data without truncation.

*Interoperability with Iceberg*: Iceberg tables are designed for interoperability across platforms (e.g., Databricks and Snowflake). The STRING type in Databricks (which has no predefined length) is mapped to Snowflake’s VARCHAR with the maximum length to accommodate any string value that might exist in the Databricks table, avoiding data loss.

*Safety and Flexibility*: Setting the length to 16,777,216 bytes (the maximum for Snowflake VARCHAR) is a conservative choice to ensure compatibility. Snowflake does this automatically because it doesn’t know the actual maximum length of the strings in the Databricks table at creation time.

 

You can override the default by explicitly defining the column’s data type and length in the CREATE TABLE statement.

 

*Why Column-Level Comments Don’t Transfer from Data Bricks to Snowflake ?*

*Metadata Handling in Iceberg*: In Iceberg, the table format used for interoperability between Databricks and Snowflake, primarily focuses on structural metadata like column names, data types, and partitioning. While Iceberg does support some metadata properties, column-level comments are not a standard part of the Iceberg schema specification that both Databricks and Snowflake universally honour. When Databricks writes an Iceberg table, it may store column comments in its own catalog (e.g., Unity Catalog), but these comments are not guaranteed to be written into the Iceberg metadata in a way that Snowflake can read.

*Snowflake’s Iceberg Implementation*: Snowflake’s Iceberg table support relies on reading the Iceberg metadata (like the schema and partition specs) from the external storage location. However, Snowflake does not currently (+*as of my knowledge*+) import or display column-level comments from Iceberg metadata, even if they exist. Snowflake prioritizes the core schema details for query execution and does not fully support extended metadata like comments in Iceberg tables. Snowflake’s own native tables support column comments via the COMMENT clause, but this is not automatically populated from external Iceberg metadata.

*Catalog Differences*: Databricks uses its own catalog (e.g., Unity Catalog or Hive Metastore) to store additional metadata like comments. Snowflake, when accessing an Iceberg table, uses its own catalog (delta_external_catalog_int in your case) to interpret the Iceberg metadata. These catalogs don’t fully align on how they handle extended metadata like comments. In your CREATE OR REPLACE ICEBERG TABLE statement, the CATALOG='delta_external_catalog_int' indicates Snowflake is using an external catalog to manage the Iceberg table, but this catalog integration doesn’t include column comments.

Work on creating an automated script to create Snowflake iceberg tables with views on top of them with column level comments is under review by [~accountid:636aa0ce96243ac755ee0558]

column197:
Connection Integration:
DBX connection should be added in all places where DIH connection is currently used.
Both connections should be initialized and handled independently.
Configuration Flags:
Introduce two flags:
isDIHEnabled: Boolean flag to enable/disable DIH connection.
isDBXEnabled: Boolean flag to enable/disable DBX connection.
Logic should respect these flags to determine which connection(s) to use.
Watcher Implementation:
Add a watcher mechanism to monitor the status of both DIH and DBX connections.
Watcher should log connection health, errors, and retry attempts.
Alerts should be triggered in case of connection failures.
Backward Compatibility:
Ensure existing DIH functionality remains unaffected when DBX is disabled.
Testing:
Unit tests and integration tests should validate both connection paths.
Test cases should cover scenarios where:
Only DIH is enabled.
Only DBX is enabled.
Both are enabled.
Neither is enabled (fallback or error handling).Successful unit test results

13/Nov/25 1:56 PM;712020:0a359ae3-9d0e-4274-bf36-9d83c8b4acbc;Please review issue with source qualifier. Vastly different record counts between DIH and Databricks.

{code:python} LEFT JOIN 
       {env}_sdh_db.sapcrm.crmd_activity_h as SDS_GCH_CRMD_ACTIVITY_H
  ON       
       SDS_GCH_CRMD_ORDERADM_H.GUID=SDS_GCH_CRMD_ACTIVITY_H.GUID AND        
       SDS_GCH_CRMD_ORDERADM_H.CLIENT=SDS_GCH_CRMD_ACTIVITY_H.CLIENT
 WHERE          
       SDS_GCH_CRMD_ORDERADM_H.PROCESS_TYPE IN('ZSTA','ZPRE') and           
       COALESCE(SDS_GCH_CRMD_ACTIVITY_H.ZZBFLD000068,' ')=' '{code}


Changing to empty string in the filter clause brings back records.

{code:sql} WHERE          
       SDS_GCH_CRMD_ORDERADM_H.PROCESS_TYPE IN('ZSTA','ZPRE') 
       and                  COALESCE(SDS_GCH_CRMD_ACTIVITY_H.ZZBFLD000068,'')=''{code}

27/Nov/25 9:01 AM;712020:ca3760a9-0eba-452e-97a1-8baf931a5e8a;*Final Conclusion:*

* In Informatica, it is taking two duplicate primary keys till the end but before loading to the target it is simply inserting the first record and ignoring the second record to maintain the primary key unique constraint.
* While databricks on the other hand is unable to handle such scenario and inserting both the records to the target and thus we get duplicates in the target. 
* To handle this scenario in databricks, I have tried implementing a logic that will behave as Informatica - Oracle relationship. 
* This will insert only the first record and ignore the second to maintain unique primary key constraint.
* But doing this too it is getting data mismatch for some records because there is no pattern for which record is getting inserted to the target.
* !image-20251127-150435.png|width=713,alt="image-20251127-150435.png"!

*Understanding through Screenshots*

* Original record present in Oracle:
* !image-20251127-151439.png|width=835,alt="image-20251127-151439.png"!

* Previously two records seen in Databricks Target after running the workflow.
* !image-20251127-151727.png|width=835,alt="image-20251127-151727.png"!

* At present, after some code changes, only one record can be seen by matching informatica/Oracle behavior with Databricks. This has dropped the second record and passed the first record to target insert.
!image-20251127-151951.png|width=835,alt="image-20251127-151951.png"!
* But as for Informatica the first input is different as per Databricks first input and there is no pattern. It drops the record according to their platform. And we still get data Mismatches.
* !image-20251128-055948.png|width=835,alt="image-20251128-055948.png"!
* !image-20251128-060102.png|width=835,alt="image-20251128-060102.png"!

* As there is no proper pattern for which data to insert in target, we will see Data mismatch for this column.

* In ORC: minimum length = 12, maximum length = 21 for contact_email_fid.


2)But For HMS not using such type of function like *ORA_HASH* That why we are getting the accurate result.

* In DBX: minimum length = 10, maximum length = 10 for contact_email_fid.
* In ORC: minimum length = 10, maximum length = 10 for contact_email_fid.

union

29/Jan/26 2:52 AM;712020:068524b1-91ea-4d3f-9fd1-67455886bf04;CDC workflows only update records that appear in the CDC transaction table for the current load window. Lookup‑based fields (like BLISTER_FLAG) are not recalculated unless that specific *material_plant_fid* is captured as an insert or update in CDC.

If the required lookup record (e.g., MARC → WERKS = 1030 with KZKRI='X') was not present during the earlier CDC load but was added later, CDC does not reprocess previously loaded rows. As a result, the old lookup value persists in the target until a full load or a future CDC event refreshes that key.

27/Jul/26 1:13 AM;712020:c614e583-7e8d-4315-a4b6-ac26f9b74b8a;The primary issue is that no historical backfill was ever performed. The 4 workflows you ran are all incremental daily workflows — they only manage CURRENT_DATE - 1 data. They cannot load historical snapshots.

Key findings:

DBX Table - 3.7M rows

DIH Source - 187M rows
column528:
27/Jul/26 5:00 AM;712020:c614e583-7e8d-4315-a4b6-ac26f9b74b8a;{{PO_PENDING_SNAPSHOT_DATE}} values in DBX do not always match DIH 

*Root Cause:* Timezone mismatch in snapshot date derivation.

* DIH (Oracle): Uses {{TRUNC(ADD_TO_DATE(SYSDATE,'DD',-1))}} which evaluates {{SYSDATE}} in the Oracle server's local timezone (e.g., US Central).
* DBX (Spark): Uses {{date_add(current_timestamp(), -1)}} which evaluates {{current_timestamp()}} based on Spark's session timezone (defaults to UTC).

When the workflow executes near midnight, the timezone difference causes a 1-day offset in the computed snapshot date between the two environments.

{code:python}WITH recon_distinct AS (

    SERIAL_NUMBER, STATUS
  FROM test_sdh_db.sapecc._scdmsdlp_recon
),
ord    AS (SELECT DISTINCT ORDER_NUMBER  FROM recon_distinct),
cli    AS (SELECT DISTINCT CLIENT        FROM recon_distinct),
vkorg  AS (SELECT DISTINCT VKORG         FROM recon_distinct),
vkbur  AS (SELECT DISTINCT VKBUR         FROM recon_distinct),
werks  AS (SELECT DISTINCT WERKS         FROM recon_distinct),
kitt   AS (SELECT DISTINCT KIT_TYPE      FROM recon_distinct),
setn   AS (SELECT DISTINCT SET_NUMBER    FROM recon_distinct),
seqs   AS (SELECT DISTINCT SEQUENCE      FROM recon_distinct),
comp   AS (SELECT DISTINCT COMPONENT     FROM recon_distinct),
lot    AS (SELECT DISTINCT LOT_NUMBER    FROM recon_distinct),
ser    AS (SELECT DISTINCT SERIAL_NUMBER FROM recon_distinct),
stat   AS (SELECT DISTINCT STATUS        FROM recon_distinct)

SELECT COUNT(*) AS row_count
FROM (
  -- 1) RECON + optional RECONH
  SELECT
    sds_cp_recon.*, sds_cp_reconh.*
  FROM test_sdh_db.sapecc._scdmsdlp_recon  AS sds_cp_recon
  LEFT JOIN test_sdh_db.sapecc._scdmsdlp_reconh AS sds_cp_reconh

    AND sds_cp_reconh.STATUS        = sds_cp_recon.STATUS

12/Jan/26 5:32 AM;712020:c91f1238-0dc8-4677-ad6c-f481c17b1fca;For primary key, duplication 
there are two tables used in source 


* *{env}_sdh_db.sapecc._scdmsdlp_reconh*
* *{env}_sdh_db.sapecc._scdmsdlp_recon*

contain identical records, which is the root cause of duplication. In Informatica, this duplication is not visible because the mapping enforces uniqueness on the primary key—only one record per key is allowed, and duplicates are dropped automatically.

The same logic has now been applied in Databricks: if two records share the same primary key, one will be discarded. Since the record that gets dropped is chosen randomly, full data validation for all rows is not feasible. Instead, validation should be performed manually on a sample set of rows.

To test the update scenario, ensure that the record exists in both source tables. If it does, one copy will be dropped during processing, which means update verification will require manual checks for selected rows.

28/Jan/26 12:29 AM;712020:595d2af5-2c65-487e-9822-11300fb2549f;The below data differences between *test_dih_db* and *dihi2_catalog* are *expected* and are due to formatting/calculation/source variations:

* *PARENT_UOM_FID* and *CHILD_UOM_FID*: In *dihi2_catalog*, the value contains an extra trailing space (example: {{"EA "}}), while *test_dih_db* has the trimmed value ({{"EA"}}). This is a whitespace/trim formatting difference only.
* *VALID_TO_DATE* and *ACTIVE_FLAG*: These fields are being *calculated correctly* in our output; however, the resulting values differ from *dihi2_catalog*. This is a data variance compared to dihi, not a calculation defect in test_dih_db.
* *GLOBAL_INDENTIFICATN_STAT_CODE*: In *dihi2_catalog*, the value appears *trimmed* (Limited to 25 characters) but the actual value is more than 25 characters, so it may not match the raw value coming from test_dih_db.
* *SEGMENTATION_VAL* and *SOURCE_DATE*: The mismatch is due to a *source data issue* (upstream/source inconsistency) rather than a transformation issue in test_dih_db.

18/Feb/26 7:36 AM;712020:2b5b834a-2559-427d-ae91-65d627e46ba9;Hi [~accountid:712020:c4d412df-dd1e-4fd2-9ceb-b974a42c5fd4] , For this object we have count mismatch for some sources in Production because of the below reasons:

# For ACH sources 
## The load workflow for ACH last ran on 9/17/2022, and  delete functionality is not implemented in the CDC workflow.
## Code relies on a NEXT_VAL stored procedure to generate the primary key dynamically. Because this sequence-based key is always generated as a new value, any updated record from the source is treated as a new insert, instead of being matched to an existing record thus increasing count
# For DHC source
## The load workflow for DHC last executed on 4/19/2021 and delete functionality is not implemented in the update workflow.This is resulting in a count mismatch between the DBX and DIH.
## There are two source queries being used, and for one of them the code relies on a NEXT_VAL stored procedure to generate the primary key dynamically. Because this sequence-based key is always generated as a new value, any updated record from the source is treated as a new insert, instead of being matched to an existing record.
# For MP source
## Source count of DBX and DIH are matching with DBX target table, since load workflow has not ran for long time in DIH and cdc workflow does not have delete functionality, DIH is having high count.

For other sources like MM,ENTPR,CTMS,MP and CP record count is not matching either because source is an ODS/ Kafka/sds tables and are not in sync with DIH
column527:
18/Feb/26 7:53 AM;712020:c4d412df-dd1e-4fd2-9ceb-b974a42c5fd4;Applicable to both ACH & DHC - In DIH as per the existing functionality in CDC workflow any record updated at the source is treated as a new record and getting inserted to the target table. In DBX this CDC workflow are deployed very recently the update history has not been carry forwarded to the target table, hence these records needs to be inserted manually into the target table.

For MP - Delete functionality is not present the existing DIH CDC workflow to handle any deletion happening at the source table and those records are still persisted in the target. Since these deleted records are not available in DBX the CDC workflow is unable to bring them to target, hence these records needs to be inserted manually into the target table.

19/Jan/26 6:52 AM;712020:55f03616-e27c-4529-9ac5-676fada91e21;The source table for this flow has  *Space vs Blank issue* for  Columns(SHTEXT_LARGE/SHORT_TEXT):
In the table *dihi2_catalog.sds_main.sds_gch_comm_prshtext*, columns like SHTEXT_LARGE and SHORT_TEXT contains 

space (' ') as a value.
However, in the ODS table *test_sdh_db.sapcrm.comm_prshtext_ods,* the same columns have blank ('') values.
where as the view *test_sdh_db.sapcrm.comm_prshtext*  which is built on this ODS table and uses a CASE statement to convert blank
values to NULL, but does not handle spaces. This leads to discrepancies during data comparison, as spaces in the dihi2_catalog
are represented as NULL in the target view(test_sdh_db.sapcrm.comm_prshtext).this issue is already reported in issue tracker to ron/brad .

07/Jan/26 12:27 AM;712020:595d2af5-2c65-487e-9822-11300fb2549f;CDC workflows are designed to capture changes from a *transaction table*, which only tracks changes in the primary source table. If the source query includes *joins with other tables*, changes in the joined tables are *not captured* in the CDC process. As a result, *joined columns in the target table retain old data* until the next full load, leading to data mismatches.

Based on the comments from Aditya, New data is required in target table so Data mismatches are expected in joined columns (primary_contact_fid, mfg_code, contact_source)

07/Jan/26 12:14 AM;712020:595d2af5-2c65-487e-9822-11300fb2549f;CDC workflows are designed to capture changes from a *transaction table*, which only tracks changes in the primary source table. If the source query includes *joins with other tables*, changes in the joined tables are *not captured* in the CDC process. As a result, *joined columns in the target table retain old data* until the next full load, leading to data mismatches.

Based on the comments from Aditya, New data is required in target table so Data mismatches are expected in joined columns (primary_contact_fid, mfg_code)

This column is flowing from a lookup (LKPTRANS) from SDS_RAD_DEVICE_CLASS_TYPE  , but when we query this table with particular ID’S, it returning nothing , so this column (REG_FDA_DVC_CLS_CD_FID) ,is returning as null in DBX as per logic .But in DIH , we have values  for this column , which is because of OLD DATA as the Load flow ran way back at “29-JUL-24”, even though the CDC flow is running daily but

*CDC workflows are designed to capture changes from a transaction table, which only tracks changes in the primary source table. If the source query includes joins with other tables, changes in the joined tables are not captured in the CDC process. As a result, joined columns in the target table retain old data until the next full load, leading to data mismatches.*

06/Jan/26 12:12 AM;712020:068524b1-91ea-4d3f-9fd1-67455886bf04;Identified an issue with the column {{SAP_CFN}} in the source qualifier query. This column is sourced from the view {{ZPLC_GTIN_XREF}} and is being matched against records from the transaction view {{CDC_SDS_CP_ZPLC_GTIN_XREF_TXN}}.

The problem is

* In {{ZPLC_GTIN_XREF}}, the column {{SAP_CFN}} contains a *blank space* for certain records.
* However, in the transaction view {{CDC_SDS_CP_ZPLC_GTIN_XREF_TXN}}, the corresponding column {{NEW_SAP_CFN}} is completely blank (no space).
* Due to this mismatch, the join condition in the source qualifier does not behave as expected.
For proper matching, the transaction view should also have a *blank space* in the {{NEW_SAP_CFN}} column wherever
 applicable, similar to the source view.

column514:
10/Feb/26 2:00 AM;712020:068524b1-91ea-4d3f-9fd1-67455886bf04;The source changed {{E1_CFN}} from NULL to space, but CDC didn’t update those legacy rows because the change happened outside the CDC transaction window processed by Informatica.
Since no new updates occurred afterward, those rows never re‑entered CDC and the target retained old NULL values.
If we run the load workflow (full/backfill) today, it will read directly from source and all NULLs in target will be replaced with spaces.
This is expected CDC behavior and requires a one‑time corrective load to sync historical records.

During the validation of records in this view, 34 rows were found to have discrepancies. The root causes are:

# Mismatched data in the source ODS between oracle and DBX.
# For the same object_status_code, multiple object_status_desc exist in the source table. Although an ORDER BY clause is applied in view definition, it cannot guarantee consistent ordering because the sort column used  is not unique which in this case is object_status_code itself. This results in mismatches between Oracle and DBX during comparison.

!image-20251226-085822.png|width=478,alt="image-20251226-085822.png"!



Case 1:

Data mismatch between CVDS view

{code:sql}%sql
select 'orc',* from dihi2_catalog.cvds_main.cvds_object_status_vw where OBJECT_STATUS_CODE='PAUS'
union
select 'dbx',* from test_dih_db.cvds_main.cvds_object_status_vw where OBJECT_STATUS_CODE='PAUS'{code}

!image-20251226-084842.png|width=705,alt="image-20251226-084842.png"!

Data mismatch between source ods table

{code:sql}select 'dbx',txt04 as object_status_code,txt30 as object_status_desc,spras from test_sdh_db.sapecc.tj02t_ods as sds_cp_tj02 where txt04 = 'PAUS' and spras='E'
union all
select 'orc', txt04 as object_status_code,txt30 as object_status_desc,spras from  dihi2_catalog.sds_main.sds_cp_tj02t as sds_cp_tj02 where txt04 = 'PAUS' and spras='E'{code}

!image-20251226-084945.png|width=705,alt="image-20251226-084945.png"!



CASE 2:

Data mismatch  between cvds view

{code:sql}select 'orc',* from dihi2_catalog.cvds_main.cvds_object_status_vw where OBJECT_STATUS_CODE='INPR'
union
select 'dbx',* from test_dih_db.cvds_main.cvds_object_status_vw where OBJECT_STATUS_CODE='INPR'{code}

!image-20251226-074241.png|width=723,alt="image-20251226-074241.png"!

Multiple rows for same object_satus_code  in source ods table

{code:sql}select 'dbx',txt04 as object_status_code,txt30 as object_status_desc,spras from test_sdh_db.sapecc.tj02t_ods as sds_cp_tj02 where txt04 = 'INPR' and spras='E'
union all
select 'orc', txt04 as object_status_code,txt30 as object_status_desc,spras from  dihi2_catalog.sds_main.sds_cp_tj02t as sds_cp_tj02 where txt04 = 'INPR' and spras='E'{code}

column1: Inbound integration (R2) - IDD2334 webmethod
column34:
*As a* developer,
*I want to* integrate a DBX (Databricks) connection wherever a DIH (Data Integration Hub) connection is used,
*So that* the system can support both data sources and allow dynamic switching or parallel usage based on configuration flags.
column197:
Connection Integration:
DBX connection should be added in all places where DIH connection is currently used.
Both connections should be initialized and handled independently.
Configuration Flags:
Introduce two flags:
isDIHEnabled: Boolean flag to enable/disable DIH connection.
isDBXEnabled: Boolean flag to enable/disable DBX connection.
Logic should respect these flags to determine which connection(s) to use.
Watcher Implementation:
Add a watcher mechanism to monitor the status of both DIH and DBX connections.
Watcher should log connection health, errors, and retry attempts.
Alerts should be triggered in case of connection failures.
Backward Compatibility:
Ensure existing DIH functionality remains unaffected when DBX is disabled.
Testing:
Unit tests and integration tests should validate both connection paths.
Test cases should cover scenarios where:
Only DIH is enabled.
Only DBX is enabled.
Both are enabled.
Neither is enabled (fallback or error handling).

column197:
User Story: Integrate DBX Connection Alongside DIH
Title: Add DBX Connection and Flags alongside DIH Connection with Watcher Implementation
As a developer,
I want to integrate a DBX (Databricks) connection wherever a DIH (Data Integration Hub) connection is used,
So that the system can support both data sources and allow dynamic switching or parallel usage based on configuration flags.
Acceptance Criteria:
Connection Integration:
DBX connection should be added in all places where DIH connection is currently used.
Both connections should be initialized and handled independently.
Configuration Flags:
Introduce two flags:
isDIHEnabled: Boolean flag to enable/disable DIH connection.
isDBXEnabled: Boolean flag to enable/disable DBX connection.
Logic should respect these flags to determine which connection(s) to use.
Watcher Implementation:
Add a watcher mechanism to monitor the status of both DIH and DBX connections.
Watcher should log connection health, errors, and retry attempts.
Alerts should be triggered in case of connection failures.
Backward Compatibility:
Ensure existing DIH functionality remains unaffected when DBX is disabled.
Testing:
Unit tests and integration tests should validate both connection paths.
Test cases should cover scenarios where:
Only DIH is enabled.
Only DBX is enabled.
Both are enabled.
Neither is enabled (fallback or error handling).
